tasks.question: Does the build-dependent half of the polynomial-matrix audit reproduce: after a fresh build of FLINT 657a2839 and the poly-prepared libraries, which pinned build artifacts differ in hash, and does a regenerated gr.s keep the audited _bf_contiguous frintn counts with no stack references?
methods: In a disposable clone, run make, then scripts/build_poly_prepared.py under new names (for example poly-prepared-rebuild-1 --prepare 1 and poly-contiguous-control-rebuild-1 --prepare 0); it refuses existing names and creates patches/<name>.patch, .deps/experiments/<name>/ and results/<name>-build/. Compare each hash in the new build.json with the pinned hash for the same role in results/poly-prepared-build/build.json and results/poly-contiguous-control-build/build.json, and recount instructions, frintn and stack references in _bf_normalize and _bf_contiguous of the new gr.s against results/poly-prepared-audit.json.

After the same build, run scripts/validate_poly_prepared.py on both new names, and a local copy of scripts/trace_poly_prepared.py pointed at the new names and a new output directory (the committed script writes to results/poly-prepared-coverage, which exists); compare test, trace and coverage counts with results/poly-prepared-audit.json.
tasks.acceptance_gate: A report giving, for each pinned build-artifact role (experiment dylib, poly-survey binary, libflint.25.0.dylib, gr.s, and trace builds if run), whether the rebuild's hash matches the pinned one, the regenerated assembly counts, the validation and coverage results, and the machine and toolchain. Hash differences are expected across toolchains and are reported, not treated as failures. Commit only a new results/ package; nothing existing changes. Recomputing summaries from raw.jsonl or re-checking patch application does not meet this gate; both are already recorded.

tasks.question: Does the prepared-input polynomial-matrix gain (4.34-15.09% CPU over 30 eligible cases) repeat when freshly built and re-measured, and does it hold on Apple Silicon other than the author's M2?
methods: Build per README.md, then scripts/build_poly_prepared.py under a new name with --prepare 1; run an unchanged-versus-unchanged control first (an unmodified library copy as candidate, as in results/poly-prepared-aa/metadata.json), then scripts/compare_poly.py with experiments/poly-prepared-confirm-plan.json twice, the second with --seed 505093, each to a new results/<name>/; report every case, including the inactive 1x1 and 2x2 controls.
Same build and control, then only the 8x8 cases of the confirm plan (the largest gains) from a new plan file with longer batches; report whether the per-case intervals overlap the stored ones.
tasks.acceptance_gate: Control intervals include zero; both runs are reported with chip, OS, compiler, FLINT commit and metadata.json hashes, whether the gain repeats or not; the report states whether the machine and GitHub account differ from the original author's, since only a different machine and contributor closes independent-replication.

first_step.scope: Positive control: the analysis and finite-model tests pass. Takes about 1 second. The FLINT build that follows takes several minutes; each confirm run is about 4,000 batches of 10-20 ms.
